reviews.review: I kind of expected ... less of this game. I'm not sure why but I was ready for this game to be really shallow and to misunderstand a lot about security and hacking. And sure, it's still sci-fi ish hacking, things have an in universe explanation and when you finish the game everything makes internal sense, which really impressed me. On top of that the experience is great. It made me feel very similarly to how uplink made me feel back in the day. Now, it's been forever since I played that so I have no idea if it holds up, but either way, this was a pleasant surprise.

Totally worth it if you are looking for a game which tells a good story and gives you a . 
It has limitations in what you can do in the shell and most hacking is done via opening ports with scripts you gather as you are "hacking" servers and checking everything out, yes.
But here is the thing: Combined with time pressure, a really good story and even non-trivial customization of your user interface, it is so much fun. Even if you know your way around computers and the internet, it is most likely that you will have fun with this game.
Just chill, put on some playlist which puts you in the vibe of being a stealthy hacker and enjoy as your bot network is spamming the targets proxy server and your scripts are tearing down ports while you try to guess or solve the firewall password.
The mission design is absolutely groundbraking, by the way. You will be using your scripts most of the time, but there are some tweaks in the details and context of the mission so every mission has a unique feel to it.
I really recommend it to at least give it a try!

First off before I get started on this review, I want it to be kept in mind that this isn't what would be called a conventional review. So if you just want to know my answer: [/b Yes, I recommend this game. It's a super enjoyable indie game if you like the concept or idea hacking.]

Now, why this review isn't conventional comes down to this review: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/SirPenguin/recommended/365450/] [/url]
First off, it's an amazing review. However I would like to argue the points he made.

[b][i]this is a casual game[/i][/b]

This game is not intended for those that want to learn programming, it's not intended for those that want to write lines of code out and debug and test it...while yes that is more realistic, what would you rather do, play a casual game and be immersed in the story and puzzles, or have to write out lines of code in order to solve the issues in front of you? (Probably spending tedious hours being bored trying to debug your code)

You'd probably prefer to use the commands the game has pre-made for you. The game design was intentional, most people wouldn't want something that get's "taken to the next level"...at least to the point of writing out lines of code by hand. In fact, most people probably won't have coding experience.

The game is a Story rich simulation game. Not a code markup tool. Not a learning game. It's made to be a fun unique puzzle game. So while regardless you'll probably find enjoyment out of the game, don't go into it expecting to find some crazy challenging puzzle that requires you to write out lines of code by hand, developing your own "hacking tools". Expect a fast pace story rich hacking game.

While I respect the points made in the above review, I felt it necessary to explain what you are really going to get out of this game, instead of a false idea of what it really is.

This game really makes you feel [strike]like batman[/strike] like a hacker. Really, that's all I can really say about this. It's a fantastic game with an amazing soundtrack that makes you feel like a badass hacker. And, if you like the base game, there's a DLC that is totally worth every cent. [i]AND[/i] There's a Steam Workshop with hundreds of great extensions and an active community (there was an event that ended just July 5th, 2020!). Seriously, if you haven't already, grab this game.

One of the best puzzle games I've played in a very long time. Hacknet might feel confusing and overwhelming at first, but it's quite intuitive once you get a grip on how it all works. Steam says it took me 12  hours to finish it because when I first played the game a few years ago I got frustrated and stopped playing half-way through. When I came back to finish it for real I started over it took about 7 hours. Hacknet is a complicated game and it can be frustrating and hard to keep track of if you're not prepared, so I'll give you some advice to help you out:

Tip 1:
Keep a pencil and a notebook with you when you play. You need to keep track of a tremendous amount of information, and you'll save yourself a lot of time and effort if you have a quick reference.

Tip 2:
Don't be afraid to look online for help if you're pulling your hair out. I often found out that I was just making typos because I misspelled something when copying down passwords or IP addresses. 

Tip 3:
When you start seeing Firewalls, Google how they work because the game doesn't do a great job explaining it. I was going to explain it here, but I didn't want to overwhelm you with a paragraph of information you won't need to know at the start of the game.

Tip 4:
The nodes on the server display seem to appear in semi-random positions and can sometimes overlap, so if  you have a program like Notepad++ I'd recommend going to 'Document/My Games/Hacknet/Accounts' then opening your save file with Notepad++, finding NetworkMap, and making it <NetworkMap sort="Grid" >. This will line up the servers in a grid in-game so they're easier to keep track of.

I was going to list some more, but I don't want to overwhelm you with too much information. 

Hacknet is a stellar puzzle game that's unlike anything else I've ever played, and I highly recommend it.

Hacknet is very satisfying. Typing out commands quickly to pretend you are some good guy hacker is quite fun. There is one mission that, due to permission on the computer, has to be completed differently than informed, but otherwise the game is excellent. It introduces new tools, and fun scenarios throughout the story that keeps it interesting. It's a nice change of pace from other games.

Game's good if you like puzzles. If you want something closer to *actual* hacking, I would suggest looking at things which aren't games, but this hacking sim's pretty fun regardless. It forces you to think more than a few times, and there's some particularly difficult challenges along the way - if you're stuck, there's always steam guides available, but they're enjoyable to solve by yourself. There's no real "endgame" after you beat the final mission though, so be warned if you're looking for something with significant replay value outside of secret/achievement hunting.

Most of the soundtrack works well, but there are two tracks (one for each end mission of base game + DLC) which really hit hard. (Roller Mobster by Carpenter Brut and Sabotage by Remi Gallego, respectively)

Doesn't take too-too long to go through, but it's still worth it. (especially while the game's on-sale)

The DLC is about the same time as the base game, can be started as soon as it's available (but getting tracekill later in the main game is helpful until you get its equivalent in the DLC) and is essentially a full sequel for the game as DLC. Missions make you think about the same or more than before, and you've got the same style of small missions and then a big long final mission [spoiler]with a race-against-the-clock final mission too[/spoiler]
DLC is, again, worth it.
